page: Amazon Web Services p3dn.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for high-performance parallel computing workloads. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8175M processor with 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with 768 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the instance features eight NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs with a combined 256 GB of VRAM.

Local storage consists of 1800 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance and high memory bandwidth, though single-core performance is relatively weak. It excels in LLM inference tasks, achieving top-tier results in prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, as well as text generation for medium and large models.

Given its dense hardware profile, the p3dn.24xlarge offers high resource density for parallel processing, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for large-scale distributed training and inference compared to deploying multiple smaller nodes. However, the trade-off includes lower single-threaded efficiency. This instance is optimized for deep learning, large language model inference, high-performance computing, and data-intensive database operations.
description: Amazon Web Services p3dn.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, featuring 96 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8175M processor and 768 GB of DDR4 memory. Designed for massive parallel processing, it integrates eight NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs with 256 GB of total VRAM, alongside 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps network bandwidth. While single-core CPU benchmarks are modest, the instance delivers strong multi-core performance and top-tier LLM inference speeds, particularly in prompt processing and text generation for medium and large models. This high-density hardware configuration is qualitatively cost-effective for complex parallel workloads, minimizing multi-node overhead. It is highly suited for deep learning, large-scale LLM inference, and high-performance computing.
